business_impact: Can create a vendor, redirect its bank account, and execute payment to it -- a fully self-contained vendor-fraud cycle with zero independent checkpoint at any stage.
suggested_mitigation: These three functions must never combine in one role. If unavoidable, require independent approval on any vendor bank-detail change before that vendor becomes payment-eligible.
status: DRAFT - not yet approved by IT Governance
notes: Escalates the existing pairwise rule P2P-VEN-01 (Change Bank Details vs Run Payment) by adding vendor creation itself into the same hands.

business_impact: Holds all three legs of the three-way match -- order, receipt, and invoice -- and can order goods that never arrive while self-certifying the entire transaction.
suggested_mitigation: Segregate at least one of the three steps to a different person. If structurally impossible for a small team, flag as a compensating-control candidate for periodic post-transaction review.
status: DRAFT - not yet approved by IT Governance
notes: Escalates the existing pairwise rules P2P-GR-02 (PO vs Goods Receipt) and P2P-INV-01 (Invoice vs Payment) by combining all three legs.

business_impact: Can create a customer, grant it an arbitrary credit limit, and sell to it -- a self-contained channel for fictitious or over-extended revenue with no independent party involved.
suggested_mitigation: Segregate customer master maintenance, credit management, and sales order entry across at least two people.
status: DRAFT - not yet approved by IT Governance
notes: Escalates the existing pairwise rule O2C-COL-03 (Credit Limit vs Sales Order) by adding customer creation into the same hands.

business_impact: Can misapply or divert a real customer receipt and cover the resulting imbalance with a credit memo, using a customer account they created themselves.
suggested_mitigation: Segregate cash application, credit memo posting, and customer master maintenance across different people.
status: DRAFT - not yet approved by IT Governance
notes: Escalates the existing pairwise rule O2C-CASH-02 (Incoming Payment vs Credit Memo) by adding customer creation into the same hands.

business_impact: Opens the account money moves through, executes the payment, and reconciles the bank statement -- complete custody of the entire payment lifecycle with no independent party at any stage.
suggested_mitigation: These three functions must sit with at least two different people. Treat as a top-priority segregation if currently combined anywhere in a real role.
status: DRAFT - not yet approved by IT Governance
notes: Escalates the existing pairwise rules TR-BANK-01 (Bank Account vs Execute Payment) and TR-OVS-01 (Release Payment vs Reconcile Bank).

business_impact: Controls a financial deal's entire lifecycle -- sets their own risk limit, books the deal, and settles it alone -- the classic 'rogue trader' scenario.
suggested_mitigation: Track as a fully organizational control (dual sign-off on deal capture, limit-setting, and settlement); none of these three functions currently has a T-code mapping in this ruleset, so no system restriction can substitute for the process control.
status: DRAFT - not yet approved by IT Governance
notes: Escalates the existing pairwise rule TR-DEAL-03 (Exposure Limit vs Deal Capture); all three legs are already Manual/Partial in the base ruleset

business_impact: Originates, capitalises, and depreciates the same asset with no independent review at any of the three major lifecycle events.
suggested_mitigation: Segregate at minimum asset master creation from capitalisation; consider periodic review of the depreciation posting log as a compensating control.
status: DRAFT - not yet approved by IT Governance
notes: Escalates the existing pairwise rule FA-MSTR-01 (Asset Record vs Capitalise/Hold) by adding depreciation execution into the same hands.

business_impact: Can physically report an asset missing (count short), approve the resulting write-off, and formally retire it -- the entire disposal-control chain in one hand.
suggested_mitigation: Require an independent physical verification and a separate write-off approver as organizational controls -- the retirement posting T-code alone is not a sufficient checkpoint on its own.
status: DRAFT - not yet approved by IT Governance
notes: Escalates the existing pairwise rule FA-PHY-02 (Count Assets vs Approve Write-off); two of the three legs have no T-code in the base ruleset.

business_impact: Posts a manual entry, approves their own posting, and reconciles/clears it away -- the entire control chain around a manual journal entry collapsed into one person.
suggested_mitigation: These three functions should never combine in one role. If any two must, ensure the third sits with someone else.
status: DRAFT - not yet approved by IT Governance
notes: Escalates the existing pairwise rules R2R-JE-01 (Post vs Approve) and R2R-JE-02 (Post vs Reconcile) by combining all three.

business_impact: Can reopen a closed period, post whatever they want into it, and sign off the close themselves -- complete control over period-end integrity.
suggested_mitigation: Restrict period open/close authority to controllership as an organizational control, and require close sign-off by someone other than the preparer of manual entries in that period.
status: DRAFT - not yet approved by IT Governance
notes: Escalates the existing pairwise rules R2R-PER-01 (Period Control vs Post) and R2R-PER-03 (Sign-off vs Post); the sign-off leg has no T-code in the base ruleset.

business_impact: Can report a stock shortfall, write it off, and also ship goods out -- the full custody-to-disposal chain in one hand, able to both cause and conceal inventory loss.
suggested_mitigation: Segregate physical counting, write-off posting, and goods issue across different people.
status: DRAFT - not yet approved by IT Governance
notes: Escalates the existing pairwise rule P2D-STK-01 (Count Stock vs Write Off) by adding goods-issue authority into the same hands.

business_impact: Self-contained production authorization from creation through confirmation, with no independent release check anywhere in the sequence.
suggested_mitigation: Segregate at least the release step from order creation and confirmation.
status: DRAFT - not yet approved by IT Governance
notes: Escalates the existing pairwise rule P2D-PRD-01 (Release vs Confirm)

business_impact: Can create a storage bin to conceal stock, move stock into or out of it, and approve their own adjustment -- a complete concealment mechanism.
suggested_mitigation: Require an independent approver for stock adjustments above a threshold as an organizational control, alongside segregating bin creation from stock movement.
status: DRAFT - not yet approved by IT Governance
notes: Escalates the existing pairwise rules EWM-CNT-02 (Adjust vs Approve) and EWM-WOF-03 (Storage Bin vs Adjust); the approval leg has no T-code in the base ruleset.

business_impact: Processes a fake or inflated return through all three steps -- receipt confirmation, crediting the customer, and posting stock back in -- with nobody else involved at any stage.
suggested_mitigation: Segregate return receipt from credit memo posting at minimum.
status: DRAFT - not yet approved by IT Governance
notes: Escalates the existing pairwise rule EWM-RTN-01 (Receive Return vs Credit Memo); Receive Return and Post Stock share the T-code MIGO

business_impact: Can build a role, grant it to anyone including themselves, and adjust the very SOD ruleset that would have flagged the combination -- arguably the single most dangerous combination in this set, since it undermines the governance process meant to catch every other rule.
suggested_mitigation: Ownership of the SOD ruleset must sit with a different person or team than role design and assignment, tracked as a governance control, not just a system restriction.
status: DRAFT - not yet approved by IT Governance
notes: Escalates the existing pairwise rules SEC-ACC-02 (Design vs Assign) and SEC-CTRL-03 (Design Role vs Maintain SoD Rules); Design Role and Assign Role also share the T-code PFCG.

business_impact: Can grant themselves emergency/firefighter access, use it, and then review -- and effectively control what gets flagged in -- the log of their own privileged session.
suggested_mitigation: Track firefighter grant, usage, and log review as a fully organizational control involving three separate people; SM20 access alone provides no real separation here, since the granting and usage steps have no T-code footprint at all.
status: DRAFT - not yet approved by IT Governance
notes: Escalates the existing pairwise rules SEC-PRIV-02 (Grant vs Use) and SEC-PRIV-03 (Use vs Review Logs) into a single three-way chain.
